In Chilliwack Downtown, the 55+ homes you can buy are Ivy Green and Spadina Regency (strata). The other seniors housing here, which you cannot buy into, is retirement residence or care and subsidized rental. This page names each building, says what type it is and what the sources show, and covers local rules and the questions buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
55+ strata buildings you can buy in Chilliwack Downtown

55+ freehold strata condo building: 24 condos, 3 storeys, built 1994, plan LMS1336, self-managed, pets not allowed. Listings describe it as a "55+ age-restricted apartment" close to downtown amenities and medical facilities. Board listing data classifies this address as "Chilliwack Downtown," which is why it is counted in this file. Confirm the age bylaw against the registered bylaws and Form B before relying on it.

55+ freehold strata condo building, concrete construction, built 1989, with secure underground parking, elevator, wheelchair access, clubhouse, workshop and a guest suite; listings state "55+ building where rentals and pets are permitted." A building directory headline records it as a 26-unit development. Unit count beyond that headline: UNCONFIRMED. Board data classifies the address as "Chilliwack Downtown," ten civic numbers from Ivy Green on the same street. Confirm the age bylaw against the registered bylaws and Form B before relying on it.
Rental, care and subsidized seniors housing in Chilliwack Downtown (not for sale)

items.t: Chartwell Birchwood Retirement Residence — 45650 Patten Avenue: Chartwell retirement residence offering independent living and assisted living, including seniors' cottages/townhouses beside the main residence. Registered in BC's Assisted Living Registry, operator Chartwell Master Care LP, class SN. Chartwell places it on Patten Avenue near the Landing Leisure Centre and Chilliwack General Hospital, with Townsend Park next door. Rental retirement living — nothing to buy.

Chartwell Hampton House Retirement Residence — 45555 Hodgins Avenue: Chartwell boutique independent-living retirement residence with care services available, one- and two-bedroom suites; the 2020 City/FVRD housing inventory records 98 units. Chartwell places it on Hodgins Avenue across from the Landing Leisure Centre and Chilliwack General Hospital, next door to Townsend Park, "on the same corner as two other Chartwell retirement residences." Rental — nothing to buy.

Chartwell Lynnwood Retirement Residence — 9168 Corbould Street: Chartwell independent-living retirement residence with care services available, studio to two-bedroom suites; Chartwell describes it as an independent living community in the heart of downtown Chilliwack, just steps from Chilliwack General Hospital, across from the Landing Leisure Centre, and on the same corner as the other two Chartwell residences above. Rental — nothing to buy.

The Cascades — 45586 McIntosh Drive: Registered in BC's Assisted Living Registry, operator Sienna-Baltic (Cascades) Inc., class SN — an assisted-living residence in the hospital precinct. BOUNDARY FLAG: whether McIntosh Drive falls inside the downtown scope or the Proper East scope is a boundary question the sources do not settle — it is carried here because the hospital precinct adjoins downtown, and it is flagged, not resolved. Care housing — you cannot buy in.

Jubilee Place (Jubilee Housing Project) — 45440 Hodgins Avenue: The 2020 City/FVRD housing inventory describes Jubilee Place as 36 units — 20 bachelor apartments and 16 one-bedroom units — offering independent retirement living to seniors 55 and over on low fixed income, with emphasis on veterans and spouses. Subsidized/non-profit rental — not ownership. Current rents and wait times: UNCONFIRMED. CONFLICT on the age note, flagged: a Chilliwack seniors resources sheet lists a 6-month to 1-year wait and a 60+ note against Jubilee Housing, differing from the inventory's 55-and-over description — confirm eligibility with the operator.

The Paramount — 46187 Yale Rd: The city's named subsidized seniors project in application material published by Chilliwack Community Services: subsidized apartments for seniors, rent calculated as 30% of monthly income, eligibility including age 65 or older, income under $39,500 and a BC Housing Registry file number, with preference given to Chilliwack residents. Subsidized rental — not ownership.

items.t: Chilliwack is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market, not a Fraser Valley or Greater Vancouver board market; CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only, with no sub-area tables, and SnapStats does not cover Chilliwack — so no market figures are stated for this area in this file: UNVERIFIED, and no other board's figures are substituted.

Municipality: City of Chilliwack, BC. The current city-wide plan is the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500; Schedule B3 is the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan covering this ground, and Schedule D-6 is the Downtown development permit area.

Working corridors, from the live page: Yale Road, Young Road, Wellington Avenue, Five Corners and First Avenue, with Highway 1 Exits 119 and 123 as its highway references. District 1881, the downtown redevelopment at the Five Corners core with heritage courtyard shops and restaurants, is the page's namesake anchor. Treat the corridors as the page's working scope only.

What the visible feed actually showed: cards read in full were all labelled "Chilliwack Downtown" — low-rise condo units (including units named in listing text as The Willows on Chesterfield Avenue and Magnolia Manor on Cheam Avenue), a detached holding property on Chesterfield Avenue described in its listing text as designated R5 in the OCP, and two strata four-plex listings on Bole Avenue — a condo-led downtown feed with infill and investment product present. The feed's total size is UNVERIFIED.

Anchor institution: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, sits west of the downtown core in the hospital precinct — Fraser Health describes it as a community hospital providing primary, core secondary and some specialty services. The downtown care cluster in (Patten Avenue, Hodgins Avenue, Corbould Street) sits within a few blocks of it.

The same file also lists Strathcona Elementary, 46375 Strathcona Rd, and Imagine High Integrated Arts/Technology, 45669 Yale Rd, both in the downtown / Yale Road corridor. Catchments are address-based — the district directs families to its School Locator — and no locator result was run for a downtown address in this research: address-level catchments UNVERIFIED.

Transit: BC Transit's service-improvements notice effective January 4, 2026 records added Sunday-evening service for Route 57 Broadway, Route 53 Fairfield and Route 51, and BC Transit's interregional routes page lists Route 66 Fraser Valley Express as serving Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby with daily service. The live page's fuller Downtown Chilliwack Exchange route list was not confirmed route-by-route beyond Routes 51, 53, 57 and 66: the remaining route numbers are UNVERIFIED in this file.

Agriculture context for the city as a whole: the City states agriculture accounts for 67% of the City's total land base and 29% of economic activity; ALR status for any specific downtown parcel is a parcel-by-parcel check.

Where 55+ housing actually concentrates in Chilliwack: the Spadina Avenue pair in this downtown scope, Mountainview Estates in Proper East, Knight Lodge and Cottage Grove on the Sardis side, and Cottonwood Village park on Evans Road — all outside this scope except the Spadina pair, listed at the end of.

blocks.text: Local rules and plans in Chilliwack Downtown

items.t: City zoning: Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000: is Chilliwack's zoning bylaw. Its defines a secondary suite as an accessory dwelling unit of not more than 90 m² and less than 40% of the habitable floor space of the building, located within a building containing only 1 principal dwelling unit — the cap is the lesser of 90 m² and 40%.

Accessory dwelling units: Section 4.06(1) of the same bylaw permits only 1 ADU per lot where the zone permits an ADU; the listed types are secondary suite, coach house and garden suite, garden suites are capped at a maximum gross floor area of 100 m² by Section 4.06(1)(g), and ADU parking is set at s.5.04 (1 space for a 1-bedroom ADU or any secondary suite; 2 spaces for a 2-or-more-bedroom coach or garden suite).

Suite legality: no secondary suite is legal unless built with a building permit meeting the BC Building and Fire Code and current flood protection requirements, and new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level.

SSMUH: Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395 is the City's small-scale multi-unit housing amendment to Bylaw No. 5000, allowing 3 to 4 dwelling units on parcels within the urban growth boundary zoned for single-detached and duplex housing; Bylaw 5395 was adopted June 18, 2024.

City plan: Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw 2025, No. 5500: is the current city-wide plan; its Schedule B3 is the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan and its Schedule D development permit areas run D-1 Drinking Water Supply through D-10 Industrial, with D-6 Downtown applying in the core — which areas apply to a given downtown parcel beyond D-6 is a per-parcel check: UNVERIFIED for any specific parcel.
Short-term rentals: the City regulates short-term rental operations under Short-Term Rental Bylaw 2021, No. 5141.

Property taxes: City of Chilliwack property tax notices are mailed annually at the end of May and are due the first working day after July 1 of every calendar year; a 5% late payment penalty is applied for taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% for taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Chilliwack Downtown

items.t: Three strata buildings share one short street, and they are three different products. On Spadina Avenue: Ivy Green (45775) is 55+ with no pets; Spadina Regency (45765) is 55+ with rentals and pets permitted; Chilliwack Gardens (45749) states "no age restrictions" in its own listing. A search that blurs the corridor will show a senior a general-market building and a pet owner a no-pets building.

The board label and the street geography name the same ground differently. Both Spadina 55+ buildings are labelled "Chilliwack Downtown" in board data while a house on the same street is labelled "Chilliwack Proper West" in listing data — a buyer who searches by sub-area label alone will find the same street filed under two different pages.

Two near-identical building names are both EAST, not downtown. Mountainview Estates (46966 Yale Rd) is the verified Proper East 55+ building; Mountview Apartments (46374 Margaret Ave) carries listing and directory language pointing the same way but stays a flagged conflict without a bylaws/Form B check. Neither belongs in downtown copy, and the two must never be merged.

One operator runs the whole hospital-corner care cluster. Chartwell operates all three retirement residences at the Landing / hospital corner — Birchwood (45650 Patten Ave), Hampton House (45555 Hodgins Ave) and Lynnwood (9168 Corbould St) — and its own copy for each notes it is "on the same corner as two other Chartwell retirement residences," so a senior comparing the three is comparing suite types and service packages inside one operator, not three competitors.
The downtown plan wording on the live page is only partly confirmed. A buyer valuing infill on that wording needs a City check, not the page copy.

A bus route's downtown service grew in 2026. BC Transit's changes effective January 4, 2026 added Sunday-evening service for Route 57 Broadway, Route 53 Fairfield and Route 51 — the downtown-side routes a senior who plans to stop driving will actually use — alongside daily Route 66 Fraser Valley Express service to Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby.

faq.q: What 55+ homes can I actually BUY in Chilliwack Downtown?
faq.a: Two verified age-restricted strata buildings, both on Spadina Avenue: Ivy Green (45775 Spadina Ave — 24 condos, built 1994, LMS1336, no pets) and Spadina Regency (45765 Spadina Ave — concrete, built 1989, rentals and pets permitted per listings).

faq.q: Three buildings share Spadina Avenue — are they all 55+?
faq.a: No. Ivy Green (45775) is 55+ with no pets; Spadina Regency (45765) is 55+ with rentals and pets permitted; Chilliwack Gardens (45749) states "no age restrictions" in its own listing. Check the civic number and the bylaws, not the street.

faq.q: Spadina Regency says rentals are permitted — in a 55+ building?
faq.a: That is what its listings state, and it is consistent with current provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. The age bylaw still governs who may RESIDE there — a tenant must meet the 55+ bylaw or an exemption — and pet rules remain a valid bylaw matter, building by building. Confirm both against the registered bylaws and Form B.

faq.q: Are The Willows or Magnolia Manor 55+ buildings?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. Both names appear in the downtown feed's listing text only, and neither was confirmed as 55+ on a developer, strata or manager source in this research — do not treat either as a 55+ purchase without the strata documents.

faq.q: Can a downtown house take a suite or a coach house for a caregiver or family?
faq.a: One accessory dwelling unit per lot where the zone permits it — a secondary suite (capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the building's habitable floor space), a coach house, or a garden suite (capped at 100 m²) — under Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000, ss. 2 and 4.06; a suite must be built with a permit meeting the BC Building and Fire Code and flood protection requirements, and new suites are not permitted below the flood construction level. Downtown parcels also sit inside the Schedule B3 Downtown Neighbourhood Plan and the D-6 Downtown permit area — confirm the parcel's designation with the City before valuing infill potential.

faq.q: If I need help later, can I stay downtown?
faq.a: The in-area ladder runs: independent strata (Ivy Green, Spadina Regency) → subsidized independent rental (Jubilee Place, 45440 Hodgins Ave, 36 units, 55+ low-income with veterans emphasis; The Paramount, 46187 Yale Rd, 65+ income-tested) → independent/assisted retirement rental in the hospital precinct (Chartwell Birchwood on Patten Ave, Chartwell Hampton House, 45555 Hodgins Ave, Chartwell Lynnwood, 9168 Corbould St) → registered assisted living (Birchwood and The Cascades, 45586 McIntosh Dr, both class SN) — all within a few blocks of Chilliwack General Hospital at 45600 Menholm Rd.

faq.q: Why are there no market numbers for this area?
faq.a: Chilliwack is a CADREB market that SnapStats does not cover, and CADREB publishes statistics board-wide only with no sub-area tables — so any Chilliwack Downtown statistic is UNVERIFIED here rather than borrowed from a neighbouring board.

faq.q: When are Chilliwack property taxes due, and what is the penalty?
faq.a: Notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1 each year; for 2026, a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026.
